summary: Use a callable overridden exec property in RegExpExec-based operations such as test and Symbol hooks.

target.notes: The RegExpExec abstract operation dynamically gets regexp.exec, calls it with the regexp as this, and requires an Object or null result.

caveats: Direct invocation of the intrinsic RegExp.prototype.exec is different: it requires RegExp internal slots and goes straight to RegExpBuiltinExec.

tests.name: test observes overridden exec
tests.input: const r=/a/; r.exec=function(s){ console.log('custom',s); return {}; }; console.log(r.test('x'));
